first.rationale: The concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding friction the most directly addressable bottleneck. Prior evidence indicates both shorter onboarding and simpler signup improved activation and time-to-value, while promotional pricing carries a documented retention cost that conflicts with sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the two onboarding records before committing to confirm the relevant intervention details and segment applicability.

final.rationale: Run a standard, randomized onboarding-shortening experiment in self-serve accounts, stratified by SMB versus other segments. It directly addresses the 4% completion and 6% activation declines, and exp_86 showed +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. Include signup-field simplification only for SMB if it is part of the treatment design: exp_31 supports SMB activation and qualified-revenue gains but showed a 1% retention decline and lacks evidence outside SMB. Evaluate qualified revenue and retention alongside completion and activation before any rollout.
